title: Jason Cohen on hidden multipliers, niching down, and building an AI company in 2026
summary: Jason Cohen explains why small systematic changes beat big investments, how to de-risk the weakest link first, why niching down sells to more than just your niche, and how WP Engine won a commodity market. He closes with how he would pick an AI product today: solve an existing problem, serve experts, and aim for 3x+ value.

principles.text: Many things must go right; tackle the weakest link first instead of building the product you already know you can build.
principles.quote: the limiting factor here is can you find customers? And if you build the product, you will have made no progress whatsoever on the question, can you go find customers?

principles.text: Niche to a narrow ideal customer; clarity about tradeoffs also wins non-ideal buyers who accept your set of weaknesses.
principles.quote: if I'm very specific about what I am then my ideal customer will definitely buy which is already a reason to do it but like 100 times larger market than that will see that specificity as a reason to buy your set of tradeoffs

principles.text: Culture and incentives of competitors can be a moat: they could copy you but won't, e.g. funded firms avoid expensive human support.
principles.quote: it's not that they couldn't have copied us, it's that they they wouldn't have because it wasn't in their nature, their culture, etc.

principles.text: Great execution wins in fields where most competitors execute poorly, even without a technical moat.
principles.quote: if you have great execution and most don't in your in your field, that's a reason to win.

principles.text: Brand is a real edge only when customers buy you despite losing on other dimensions; it follows execution, and consistency matters more than the specific logo.
principles.quote: how do you tell when brand is really starting to matter either competitively at all or maybe a moat as opposed to just the identity of the thing like a handle of the thing is when customers are making buying decisions because of it.

principles.text: Commodity products escape commodity status by being many multiples better (4x faster, not 30%), which you can feel immediately.
principles.quote: when it's not just quote unquote better or faster, more efficient, cheaper, but five times better, three times cheaper D, right? Where you could measure it, but like you don't even need to to see like, holy crap
